items.title: Bob Rosengarden interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, October 6, 1996
items.q: Of course he fired me. He fired me many times... the last time we worked together was a long time ago

ctx.x: Well you have to be fairly accomplished.

Oh, yeah, Benny was a wonderful player. Of course he fired me. He fired me many times, I mean he fired everybody. One story I remember he called me, and he had a strange voice on the phone, “Bobby” I mean his voice, “Bobby, this is Benny.” And I said, “Yes, I know.” He said, “Bobby, tell me something?” True story. And I said, “What is it, Benny?” He says, “Am I mad at you?” And I said, “I beg your pardon?” And he said, “Am I mad at you? I seem to remember that I’m mad at you.” I said, “I don’t think so, Benny,…
mind, can you do—” such-and-such. And then he never called me again. I mean then I did the job, whatever it was, and he just [inaudible]. But, “Bobby, am I mad at you?”
